Button.reason: Ember's Button only adds `cds--layout--size-{size}`; @carbon/react's Button also adds a `cds--btn--{size}` modifier class (e.g. `cds--btn--lg`) that Ember's component never emits for non-default sizes. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

Same `cds--btn--{size}` gap as `cds--btn--lg` above, for the `md` size - deliberately left component-wide (no `variant` scoping) since six of the nine Button variants legitimately render at the default `md` size; note that this also means a future genuine `cds--btn--md` regression on any of them would be silently swallowed too, same tradeoff already accepted for `cds--btn--lg`.
Same `cds--btn--{size}` gap as `cds--btn--lg` above, for the `sm` size.
Same `cds--btn--{size}` gap as `cds--btn--lg` above, for the `xl` size.

Ember's <button> template sets `aria-label='{{if @type "danger"}}'`, which renders aria-label="danger" whenever @type is any truthy string (i.e. on every button, since @type defaults to 'primary') instead of only on an actual danger/icon-only button. @carbon/react's Button never sets aria-label here at all. Looks like an unintended bug in the Ember template, tracked as a follow-up rather than fixed in this DOM-parity-test PR.

Ember's `primary` getter is `args.primary || args.type === 'primary'`; @type still defaults to 'primary' when only @tertiary={{true}} is passed (there is no separate 'off' value), so `cds--btn--tertiary` and `cds--btn--primary` are both added instead of just `cds--btn--tertiary`. @carbon/react's `kind='tertiary'` only ever adds `cds--btn--tertiary`. Real bug, tracked as a follow-up.
Same `type` defaults to 'primary' bug as the `tertiary` variant above, for @ghost={{true}} - `cds--btn--ghost` and `cds--btn--primary` both get added. Real bug, tracked as a follow-up.

Tag.reason: @carbon/react's Tag sets `title` on the `.cds--tag__label` span (used for a truncation tooltip); Ember's Tag never sets it. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.
@carbon/react's Tag sets `dir='auto'` on the `.cds--tag__label` span; Ember's Tag never sets it. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

@carbon/react's Tag spreads `disabled` straight onto its root element regardless of tag type, so a non-interactive (div-rendered) disabled Tag still carries a `disabled="true"` attribute alongside the `cds--tag--disabled` class. Ember's Tag only ever adds the class, never the attribute. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

Loading.reason: Ember's inline branch hardcodes `style='margin-left: 1rem; width: initial; display: inline-flex; align-items: center;'` on the root div; @carbon/react's InlineLoading sets no inline style at all (its layout comes entirely from `cds--inline-loading`'s own CSS). Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.
Same hardcoded inline-style gap as `margin-left` above.
Same hardcoded inline-style gap as `margin-left` above.
Same hardcoded inline-style gap as `margin-left` above.

@carbon/react's InlineLoading renders its inner spinner via `Loading` with no `aria-atomic`; Ember's inline branch hardcodes `aria-atomic='true'` on that div (copied from the non-inline branches). Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

Ember's inline branch puts `aria-label={{@description}}` on both the spinner div and its svg; @carbon/react's InlineLoading only ever puts a label on the svg (via its own `iconDescription`/`status` fallback), never on the wrapping div. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

@carbon/react's InlineLoading passes its own `iconDescription` (defaulting to the literal string "loading", NOT `description`) to the inner spinner's aria-label/title - `description` only ever reaches the separate visible text below. Ember's inline branch has no separate `iconDescription` concept and reuses `@description` for both, so the icon's label differs from React's default whenever a caller passes a real @description. Real gap, tracked as a follow-up.

Loading.path: div > div[0] > div[0] > svg[0] > title[0] > text("loading")[0]
Loading.reason: Same `iconDescription` vs `description` gap as the svg aria-label above - the <title> text mirrors whichever value was actually used for the label.
